subject: mechanical
audience: FE Mechanical candidates and mechanical engineering students
title: The Thin-Wall Vessel That Saw 100 MPa Hoop Stress
featured_title: THE THIN-WALL VESSEL THAT SAW 100 MPA HOOP STRESS

presentation.challenge: At 2 MPa internal pressure, the vessel's hoop stress reached 100 MPa—twice the longitudinal stress.

practice.primary_question: Why is hoop stress twice longitudinal stress in a thin-walled cylindrical pressure vessel?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Using the same membrane-stress formula for both circumferential and longitudinal directions.

case_dna.target_misconception: Thin-walled cylindrical vessels have the same membrane stress in the hoop and longitudinal directions.
case_dna.why_plausible: Both stresses are caused by the same internal pressure, so equal values can seem intuitive.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: For p=2 MPa, D=1.0 m, and t=10 mm, hoop stress pD/(2t)=100 MPa while longitudinal stress pD/(4t)=50 MPa.
case_dna.corrected_model: For a thin-walled closed cylinder, hoop stress is twice longitudinal stress.

problem_statement: A thin-walled cylindrical vessel has internal pressure 2.0 MPa, internal diameter 1.0 m, and wall thickness 10 mm. A design note uses 50 MPa for both membrane directions. Calculate hoop and longitudinal stresses and identify which direction governs.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: One pressure produced two different membrane stresses.
gates.cta: Cut the vessel in two directions

options.label: Use σh=pD/(2t) and σL=pD/(4t)
options.reason: Circumferential and longitudinal equilibrium produce different membrane-force relations.

options.label: Use σh=σL because pressure is the same in every direction
options.reason: Pressure is isotropic, but the vessel equilibrium areas and resisting wall sections differ.

options.label: Longitudinal stress is twice hoop stress
options.reason: For a thin-walled closed cylinder, hoop stress is the larger one.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the hoop stress
gates.prompt: What is the hoop stress in MPa?

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Pressurize the cylinder
gates.result: The hoop stress is 100 MPa; longitudinal stress is 50 MPa.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove both membrane stresses
gates.prompt: Calculate σh=pD/(2t) for p=2 MPa, D=1.0 m, t=0.01 m. Enter MPa.
gates.hint: Use consistent units and the thin-wall formulas.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Membrane equilibrium identifies the governing direction

cards.text: The hoop direction governs because its membrane stress is twice as large.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the vessel-stress note
report: C3. Hoop and longitudinal membrane stresses are both 50 MPa.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: The two stress directions use different equilibrium relations.

evidence_choices.label: σh=100 MPa while σL=50 MPa
evidence_choices.reason: This follows from thin-wall cylindrical equilibrium.

correction.template: The hoop stress is {hoop} MPa and longitudinal stress is {longitudinal} MPa.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Reduce hoop stress to 50 MPa at the same pressure and diameter
gates.constraint: Keep p=2 MPa and D=1.0 m.

options.label: Increase wall thickness to 20 mm
options.reason: Hoop stress is inversely proportional to wall thickness.

options.label: Keep 10 mm and use the longitudinal formula for hoop stress
options.reason: The physical hoop stress does not change with formula selection.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply thin-wall scaling
gates.prompt: If wall thickness doubles while pressure and diameter stay fixed, what happens to hoop stress?

options.label: It stays unchanged
options.reason: Membrane stress depends directly on thickness.

gates.explanation: Thin-wall membrane stress is inversely proportional to wall thickness.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the vessel model
gates.confirmation: I confirm that hoop and longitudinal stresses in a thin-walled closed cylinder are different and must be checked separately.

items.label: What failed
items.value: Both vessel stress directions were assigned the same value.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: Different membrane-force equilibrium in hoop and longitudinal cuts.

seo.seo_title: Thin-Wall Pressure Vessel Hoop Stress: 100 MPa vs 50 MPa | FE E-059
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Mechanical Case E-059: a 2 MPa, 1 m diameter, 10 mm wall cylinder has 100 MPa hoop stress and 50 MPa longitudinal stress.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Mechanical pressure vessel hoop stress
seo.excerpt: A thin-walled cylinder does not carry equal membrane stress in both principal directions. Hoop stress is twice longitudinal stress.
seo.direct_answer: For a thin-walled closed cylinder, σh=pD/(2t) and σL=pD/(4t). With p=2 MPa, D=1 m, and t=10 mm, hoop stress is 100 MPa and longitudinal stress is 50 MPa.

faqs.q: Which stress is larger in a thin-walled cylindrical vessel?
faqs.a: Hoop stress; it is twice the longitudinal stress in the idealized closed-cylinder model.

faqs.q: How does wall thickness affect hoop stress?
faqs.a: Hoop stress is inversely proportional to wall thickness.
